newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Bunker sales gave further boost.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Bunker sales gave further boost.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices edged up slightly as the emergence of new buying interest and refinery output cuts gave the market a boost, traders said on Monday.
They said there are healthy supplies in the market but sales in the bunker market has picked up and this has helped to move excess volumes from the cargo market.

"Previously, shipowners were unwilling to buy as they expected cargo prices to fall further, but now prices have tipped upwards, buyers who were caught are now covering their requirements," said a bunker player.
"Bunker volumes have provided some support," said a cargo trader.
Others said they still see good supplies from Mideast and South Korea. South Korean cargoes for Februray loading were offered at a 50 cents premia over Singapore spot quotes.
At least six Iranian cargoes, the usual term supplies from Iran were heard to be heading towards Singapore. Most of this supplies will be sold in the bunker market, traders said.
A European trader was heard to be bringing two Kuwaiti spot cargoes and a mideast bunker trader four cargoes.
Traders said the depressed market in Mideast had triggered the movement of supplies here.
Another trader said the current depressed European market "is not helping".
Late Monday, a bid was seen at $99 per tonne against offers at $101 for February loading supplies from Singapore.
